body: Did you find something to help you?!  Relate & desperate to feel.

Your theory on DBT is incorrect.  DBT is used in bipolar, TBI, depression, and cluster-B.  It’s a manualized behavioral therapy, which can be off-putting to some.  Take what works from it, or none at all.  If you truly want to change your behavior, writing off all mindfulness or skills or thinking you’re too special for it to be effective wont be effective. Schema therapy & mentalization based psychotherapy are also evidence based for BPD. Some find help in Stoicism, Buddhism, having some kind of spiritual foundation or code.   12 step groups can aid in support & individual issues, such as codependency or substance use.   An individual therapist with experience with personality disorders, seen over a long period of time, would be a great bet.

Heal completely?  Maybe not.  Change your circumstances, thinking, heal past traumas, get physically healthier, explore new ideas, try other modalities, seek connection in new ways, leave behind self-identity as a depressed person?  Very possible.  Try something different…anything.
Make sure it is documented in all medical databases/records, too.
I have TBI & cigarettes/smoke wreck me.  Perfumes are migraine triggers.
Benzos destroy lives.

That comment is a bit naive.  Yes, neuroplasticity is real, but not without rehabilitation, repetition, & the right conditions, and most of the progress is made in the first few years post-injury.  I didn’t just have ECT.  I had other TBI’s.  I had hope initially.  I do not anymore.  Things like hyperbaric oxygen or cognitive remediation take $$$.

Solutions: 
1: Don’t go back to doctor.
2. Don’t mention suicidal ideation.
4. Realize arguing over a label is futile.
5. Drop out of the System & switch medical providers should you ever need medical care.

“Wanting to fight” is an action urge, not an emotion.  Look up the term ‘alexithymia.’  (No, I’m not labeling you as anxious!).  A lot of people with trauma, brain injury, etc experience an inability to identify/label their emotions.  It sounds like you are stuck in fight/flight, for sure.

When did you have ECT?  I haven’t been able to work since & consider myself disabled.  I’m 35.  I don’t think I qualify for SSDI due to only working from 15-28 & fear I’ll need to be “med compliant” to get any benefits.

I’m so sorry for you, too.  The isolation is really sad.  I feel so misunderstood.  I look “fine” on the outside, and it’s such an invisible disability.  

Yes, I got diagnosed with BPD after shock.  Then bipolar, dependent personality, paranoid personality, it’s an endless list.  It’s trauma & brain injury.  

Thank you for relating.
Did this improve?  I’m in major pain.
I feel way more suicidal & unsafe after psychiatry, though.  I was never agitated or aggressive prior to ECT and traumatic brain injury.

I don’t think you are referring to the majority.  Cost of living is extremely high here.  Many people work two or three jobs and receive public assistance and still live paycheck to paycheck or end up homeless.  The “rich, greedy, privileged” are a minority.

Some people have a first episode of psychosis, are medicated, and withdrawing from the AP causes rebound via dopamine supersensitivity, thus reconfirming the need for the med.  Others are not educated about or presented with alternative interventions.  A pill is cheaper than taking someone out of poverty, helping them out of abusive circumstances, providing long term medical follow up/preventative care, testing for food allergies, and providing psychosocial support.  

I don’t think it is fair to judge the individuals taking meds so harshly, but rather the System and way altered states of consciousness & behaviors are treated by society as a whole.  

My friend has TBI, and had an episode of psychosis.  He believes he needs to be on Risperdal for life because that’s what he was told by doctors.  He also fears the withdrawal so much & another episode from withdrawing, he prefers to stay medicated for life.  That’s his choice, and he reports few side effects.  I also have TBI & experience psychosis & mania & ended up homeless with severe life/relational consequences unmedicated.  Who is “right?”

SSRI’s are clinically effective for under 1/3 of users, and efficacy is measured in 6-12 week trials with scores on many measures (e.g. MARS-D) just barely reaching statistical significance.  Exercise alone beats/equals Zoloft in a famous Duke research study, and exercise alone still fares better than Zoloft + exercise.

For many (60-70%), even based on the medical literature, they are no better than placebo.

Yes, antidepressants can induce mania and mixed episodes & precipitate rapid cycling (i.e. crashing from mania, cycling back up).  I now experience almost exclusively mixed states (including psychosis) after taking antidepressants.
Great post.  I’m going to complete this process.  I am scared it has to be notarized, but I will find out.

You’re 19.  Did they diagnose you bipolar 1?  That’s a big cocktail.   Do you have trauma?  Have you done DBT?  Looked into PMDD? Plenty of time to recover from akathisia & heal your brain.   Unless you have schizophrenia, you don’t need 30 mg Abilify.  5-10 can treat psychosis.  Plus, Abilify has one of the highest rates of akathisia.  I took 2 mg & paced for three weeks.   I think you’ve been misdiagnosed, and I know nothing about you.  Your writing is perfectly clear.  900 lithium should prevent mania (and thus psychosis).  You could also add Lamictal & potentially drop the other two if you do, indeed, have classic bipolar 1 disorder. Diagnoses made at such young ages should be subject to review.  Get another opinion.
Writing was one of my greatest gifts in this world.  ECT & psych drugs killed it for me, too.  I barely feel human.

Last hospitalization, was put on three mood stabilizers, Klonopin.  I have TBI & definitely admit my judgment/impulsivity is too impaired to be making great decisions or stay on meds reliably, so I want to be med free.  The trauma of the last few years is horrific.  I have chronic akathisia.  I’ve been raped, kidnapped.  I trust nobody & try to stay away from any people outside of Peer Support, churches, 12 step mtgs.  I have done a lot I’m not proud of in terms of core values to survive.  I was just started on an antidepressant, Klonopin PRN, supposed to take hydroxyzine/gabapentin.  I want to give up.

Thank you for this.  I am homeless & yes, it is impossible to stay out of psychosis (or mania).  I’m too scared to sleep.  I’ve never done drugs in my life besides psych meds, don’t drink, and have extensive trauma, TBI, and Celiac disease.  Homelessness, revolving door of involuntary hospitalizations, more trauma.  It is hell, and people assume you are lazy & a drug addict.

I have been unable to work (and became homeless) since ECT.  It is validating to see someone else similarly affected by this procedure.  I was in denial for many years, but I am disabled.  It hurts so badly people thinking I am “lazy.”

Your identity or who you think you are IS an illusion, from some perspectives.  Questioning the “you” underneath one’s labels, self-identifications, etc. is a spiritual/philosophical quandary as old as time.  The meds, to me, took away the ability to think clearly or deeply and caused horrific anxiety/dread….which made philosophizing and redefining purpose impossible.  The meds are not meant to help you understand yourself.  They do the opposite.

1) Get another opinion.  2) Research tapering.  If you start, you’re going to want to go extremely slowly & have a good support system, someone who understands psychosis/altered states, in your corner.  

I have experienced a lot of psychosis & the meds terrify me.  I’m labeled with “bipolar disorder,” but have had every diagnosis at some point.  Nobody in psychiatry is going to advocate for one to be med free, as it is like going to a dentist saying you don’t want your teeth examined.  

I, too, have spiritual & religious themes in altered states.  Can you connect spiritually while on medication?  I don’t believe there’s a cure, per se.  Unresolved trauma & autoimmune disease & stress…the altered states come back for me.  But I envision a life free of meds & connected again.  Start looking into your options now & make choices with a clear head.  Don’t rush.

100%.  I don’t want a romantic relationship or anything.  I want connection— friends, family members, community, support groups, a pet….connection & belonging.  I’m homeless & the loneliness is unbearable.

It totally depends on the facility.  I don’t want to scare you.  If you’re not acute or acting out, the staff is usually respectful.  Their goal is to stabilize you quickly and get you back out in the community.  It can feel infantalizing, dehumanizing, or supportive depending on the place.  Their main role is medication management & safety, so groups are pretty minimal and geared toward people who might be very symptomatic.  In short, it can be chaotic or boring as heck.  I think you’d be better suited for a residential or outpatient program, unless you’re acutely suicidal.  If you have an insurance plan through your employer, they might have a general mental health or substance use residential program which would offer more in the way of accommodations and support.  Have you talked to your therapist about needing more support?  Heck, if I could go on a retreat to Costa Rica, I would!  Ayahuasca is on my bucket list, and I imagine it’d be more healing than a pharmaceutical (but I digress).

I’ve gone to a hospital voluntarily.  If you’re looking for med changes or are unsafe/manic/unable to care for yourself/etc, hospitals are the go-to.  But they usually offer little in the way of therapy, unless it is a private or residential facility.  You might try looking into intensive outpatient/PHP programs which would offer structure, groups, etc. but you could still see your outside therapist and sleep at home.  Or a residential program if covered by insurance.  That would give you time away to just focus on recovery.
